thesis: Verisk Analytics (Nasdaq: VRSK), data analytics for insurance. Q3 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-11-05) read. Q3 revenue 809.0M (+5.3%), 9M 2,397.9M (+4.5%); Q3 net income 219.2M vs 225.5M; Q3 OCF 267.2M vs 403.5M. Close 202.09 (2026-11-20) x 128,249,862 shares (2026-09-30 balance sheet) = 25.9B = 29.5x TTM NI 879.2M (908.3-711.1+682.0); TTM FCF 1,100M (OCF 1,366.9 less capex 266.5) = 4.2%. Debt 4,495M vs cash 557M; stockholders' deficit -1,114M after 2026 buybacks (9M financing outflow 2,416M including repayment of 1.5B AccuLynx-related notes). AccuLynx: Delaware Chancery (2026-08-07, final order 08-14) found Verisk breached the merger agreement and ordered specific performance; Delaware Supreme Court affirmed 2026-10-23 (8-K filed 10-29). Verisk must use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain FTC clearance and close, so a deal it tried to terminate may still complete; price, size and financing were not read here. The 1.5B notes issued for it were redeemed.
counterthesis: Growth is only about 5% against a 29.5x earnings multiple; Q3 profit and OCF fell year on year. Negative equity and 4.5B debt leave less cushion if a forced AccuLynx closing needs new financing after the 1.5B notes were redeemed. Legal outcome compelled an acquisition Verisk tried to exit, a governance and capital allocation concern. Price fell from 212.76 (11-16) to 202.09. OCF 9M -6.3%. Missing: organic growth, margins and EBITDA.
invalidation: Downgrade if forced AccuLynx closing adds leverage or FTC conditions, organic growth stays near 5% while multiple holds, or OCF keeps falling; upgrade case needs peers (SPGI, MCO, FICO, CoStar), organic growth, EBITDA margin and verified quote origins.
